claims.text: This trip deviates from the route the rider booked. The GPS trace runs 11.18 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 8.2 km — an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.34% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute), so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED, and POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure — 11.18 km, not the rounded 11.2 km convenience copy — the governing measurement.

The rider's complaint is not that a detour happened — the closure explains that — but that the detour cost them ERP they never agreed to. The route they booked carries no ERP at all: trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00, and the routing engine records the optimal route as 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry'. Every cent of the $4.00 of ERP on this fare was created by leaving that no-gantry corridor; none of it belongs to the trip the rider booked.

Both charged gantries are itemised in the fare breakdown as lying off the optimal route: CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at $1.00, each carrying on_optimal_route false, with the breakdown's own on-optimal-route ERP total at $0.00 and its off-optimal-route total at $4.00. The trace confirms the vehicle actually passed both points (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 40.2 m). These are genuine off-route pass-through charges for gantries that form no part of the booked route, and they are precisely what the rider contests.

The LTA DataMall closure EV-ADVIS-00103-01 exonerates the distance and time charges under POL-RD-03: it names Braddell Road between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd, its 05:30–12:00 window overlaps the trip, and its geometry intersects the booked optimal route. But exoneration of the driver's conduct does not shift the government-set pass-through onto the rider. Under POL-RD-09(2), where a deviation is exonerated as an external event, off-route ERP is still refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at SGD 12.00 per trip. The rider did not cause the closure any more than the driver did, and the $4.00 of gantry charges they never chose must come back.

The $4.00 is refundable whichever way the closure is treated, so no reading of the record leaves it with the rider. If POL-RD-03 exoneration applies, POL-RD-09(2) returns it as a pass-through correction. If the judge declines to exonerate, POL-RD-09(1) and POL-RD-02 still return it, because a recomputed fare built on the optimal route (16.63) contains ERP for on-optimal-route gantries only — here 0.00 — so the $4.00 is comprehended inside the refund and is never added on top. Either route to the ruling ends with the rider whole on the ERP.

The driver cannot move this ERP to the rider under POL-RD-04, because the chat runs the other way. At 08:12:30 the driver announced 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah'; the rider's only message is 'ok' at 08:12:58 — an acknowledgment of the driver's choice, not a rider instruction. POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider and to identify a place or road specifically enough to act on, corroborated through chat_message.waypoint_hint; the rider's message carries no waypoint_hint, so the corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable on this record, and POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP refund.

The rider has carried the initial POL-RD-08 burden and it has shifted. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-00103, and the unimpaired trace shows an excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold. To resist, the driver must point to a specific artifact and clause; the only exculpatory artifact on file — the closure advisory — is directed at the distance and time lines, not at the $4.00 of ERP the rider is disputing, and it discharges nothing on those pass-through lines.

claims.text: The road closure fully exonerates this route under POL-RD-03. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00103-01 (ADV-20260714-031, severity HIGH) closes 'Braddell Road (towards Serangoon), between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd' from 05:30 to 12:00 on 2026-07-14, and the trace window (first fix 08:07:20, last fix 08:36:20) sits squarely inside that window. The POL-RD-03 cap is min(measured excess 2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km) = 2.98 km. The whole of the measured excess is therefore justified, nothing is left unexonerated, and the driver keeps the fare computed on the closure-adjusted optimal.

All three POL-RD-03 conditions are met on this record: (a) the advisory names a road the optimal route traverses - the trip_record's own optimal_route_source is 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry', the same Braddell Road the advisory closes; (b) its validity window overlaps the time the trace shows the vehicle on that segment (intersects_route true, overlaps_trip_window true, overlap_minutes 35.2); and (c) the driven line leaves the optimal corridor and rejoins it, running 11.18 km against an 8.2 km optimal, crossing two CTE gantries each flagged on_optimal_route false, exactly the 'Diversion via Lorong 1 Toa Payoh or CTE' the advisory describes. The driven 11.18 km is within 0.58 km of the 10.6 km shortest lawful alternative, inside the 1.0 km tolerance built into the POL-RD-03 cap.

Because POL-RD-03 fully excuses the excess, POL-RD-02 does not run against the rider's benefit. POL-RD-02 is engaged only where a deviation is established AND 'no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'; here the exculpatory clause excuses 100% of the excess. POL-RD-03 directs POL-RD-02 only to the excess BEYOND the cap, and there is none. The driver was not at fault for an emergency water-main closure, so the distance and time charges stand and no distance-based refund is owed to the rider.

The rider's only recovery is the off-route ERP pass-through under POL-RD-09(2): where the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03 the distance and time charges stand, but off-route ERP is refunded standalone, capped at SGD 12.00. The off-route ERP actually charged is SGD 4.00 (CTE Braddell Rd SGD 3.00 plus CTE Moulmein Rd SGD 1.00, both on_optimal_route false; off_optimal_route_total 4.00, on_optimal_route_total 0.00). The correction is therefore SGD 4.00 - not the SGD 9.00 contested, and not the SGD 8.50 that an UNadjusted POL-RD-02 recomputation against the booked 8.2 km optimal would yield. The closure is worth roughly SGD 4.35 to the driver and that reduction is exactly what POL-RD-03 exists to deliver.

Neither ERP line is a phantom charge, so POL-RD-09(4) adds nothing to the rider's recovery. Under the POL-RD-09 match rule a gantry is treated as crossed where a trace fix lies within 250 m of it: the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry at (1.3401, 103.8496) has a nearest fix at 0.0 m (fix index 33, 08:12:50) and the CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) gantry at (1.324, 103.854) has a nearest fix at 40.25 m (fix index 74, 08:19:40), both well inside the radius, and both charge times (08:14:06 and 08:19:41) fall inside the trace window. There is no unmatched line, no billing-integrity failure, and no ground for a full ERP refund on top of the capped pass-through.

The rider had contemporaneous notice of the diversion and did not object. At 08:12:30 the driver messaged 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' and the rider replied 'ok' at 08:12:58, both read within about 30 seconds; that exchange predates the second gantry charge at 08:19:41. It corroborates that the diversion was the driver's response to the closure, not a route taken against the rider's wishes, and it is consistent with the advisory the platform elsewhere holds.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern and no POL-RD-06 uplift. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 553 - below the 3-flag test and below the 0.05 ratio test - so no pattern is established and neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor the driver-conduct referral of POL-RD-06 follows. The deviation is in any event not MATERIAL on this trip (36.3% and 2.98 km, both under the 50% and 8.0 km thresholds), so the POL-RD-06 check was not even required. POL-GEN-01 confines any profile use to these named counters; the driver's record is not a ground for an adverse finding.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07, so there is no route to ESCALATE. It carries 175 fixes at a 10.0 s sampling interval with 100% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0; limbs (a) to (c) are not engaged and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation ground is closed. The excess rests on a clean, unbroken trace and the case can and should be decided on this trip's own evidence rather than held for a human reviewer.

Even on the tribunal's alternative reading the rider's recovery is bounded at SGD 4.15. The driver has discharged the POL-RD-08 shifted burden by pointing to a specific advisory ID (EV-ADVIS-00103-01) and a specific clause (POL-RD-03), so the excess is excused rather than refunded. If the tribunal prefers to run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal of 11.18 km instead, the refund is charged_total 25.12 less recomputed_fare 20.993 = 4.127, rounded up to SGD 4.15 - and that figure already excludes the off-route gantries, so the ERP cannot be counted a second time (POL-RD-09(1)). Either way the rider is far short of the SGD 9.00 contested.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties:

WHAT WAS DECIDED
This trip TRP-00103 did deviate, but the deviation is fully excused, and the one thing the rider actually paid for that was never part of their route — the $4.00 of CTE ERP — is refunded. The rider asked for $9.00; the evidence supports $4.00.

THE DEVIATION (established but not material)
The GPS trace runs 11.18 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 8.2 km — an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.3%. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (above 20% and above 0.8 km), so the deviation is established. It is not MATERIAL (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so no driver-conduct check was even required. The governing measurement is the trace figure 11.18 km, not the rounded 11.2 km on the trip record.

THE CLOSURE EXONERATES DISTANCE AND TIME (POL-RD-03)
The LTA DataMall closure EV-ADVIS-00103-01 meets all three POL-RD-03 conditions: it names Braddell Road, which the booked optimal route uses ('Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry'); its 05:30–12:00 window overlaps the trip; and the trace leaves that corridor and rejoins it. The justified excess is min(measured 2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 − 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km) = 2.98 km — the whole of the measured excess. Nothing survives the exoneration, so POL-RD-02 does not run: no distance-and-time refund is owed, and the driver keeps the fare for distance and time. The driver's figures here are accepted.

THE ERP IS RETURNED (POL-RD-09(2))
Where a deviation is exonerated as an external event, POL-RD-09(2) still refunds off-route ERP to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at SGD 12.00. Both charged gantries (CTE Braddell Rd $3.00, CTE Moulmein Rd $1.00 = $4.00) are itemised on_optimal_route false, and the trace passes each within the 250 m match radius (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 40.2 m), so neither is a phantom charge and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises. Refund = $4.00, below the $12.00 cap. The rider's point that their booked route carried no ERP at all (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00) is accepted and is why this sum comes back.

WHY NOT $4.15, AND WHY NOT $9.00
The driver's alternative figure of $4.15 (charged_total 25.12 less a recomputed fare 20.993 run against the closure-adjusted optimal) is not the governing computation: POL-RD-03 fully exonerates the excess, so POL-RD-02 has nothing to run against, and the pass-through limb fixes the correction at the off-route ERP actually charged, $4.00. The residual ~$0.13 is meter rounding on distance and time that stands with the exonerated fare. The rider's $9.00 is not supported beyond the $4.00 of ERP.

THE CHAT DOES NOT MOVE THE ERP (POL-RD-04 unavailable)
The driver announced 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' at 08:12:30 and the rider replied 'ok'. That is an acknowledgement of the driver's decision, not a rider instruction, and the message carries no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable. The $4.00 is therefore not converted into a rider-caused detour under POL-RD-09(3).

INTEGRITY AND PROFILE
The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 175 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — limbs (a)–(c) of POL-RD-07 are not engaged, so no POL-RD-10(3) escalation. The driver profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 across 553 completed trips in 90 days: no repeat pattern, so no POL-RD-06 uplift and no driver-conduct referral. All admitted artifacts carry weight 1.0, which is the cap on this ruling's confidence.

OUTCOME: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 4.00 (the off-route ERP pass-through). Charged_total SGD 25.12; no distance-and-time refund runs; the rider's remaining charge stands.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties agree on the essentials, and the tribunal accepts them.

DEVIATION (POL-RD-01). The GPS trace EV-GPS-00103 runs 11.18 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against the booked optimal of 8.2 km on EV-TRIP-00103 — an excess of 2.98 km, 36.34% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is established. The trace figure, not the rounded 11.2 km convenience copy, governs. The deviation is not MATERIAL (36.34% is under 50%, 2.98 km under 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 profile check was not required.

CLOSURE EXONERATION (POL-RD-03). The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00103-01 closes 'Braddell Road (towards Serangoon), between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd' — the very arterial the trip_record's optimal_route_source names for the no-gantry optimal route. Its 05:30–12:00 window overlaps the trip, and the driven line leaves that corridor onto the CTE and rejoins after. The cap on exoneration is min(2.98 km, 1.30 × (10.6 − 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km) = 2.98 km, so the whole measured excess is justified. Nothing is left unexonerated, POL-RD-02 does not run, and the distance and time charges stand. The driver advocate's alternative figure of $4.15 (POL-RD-02 run against the closure-adjusted optimal) does not arise: that computation applies only to excess beyond the POL-RD-03 cap, and there is none.

THE $4.00 OF ERP (POL-RD-09). This is the live dispute and the rider wins it. The booked route carries no ERP at all (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00), and both charged gantries — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) $1.00 — are itemised on_optimal_route false, with the breakdown's on-optimal total at $0.00 and off-optimal total at $4.00. Both gantries are genuinely crossed: nearest fixes at 0.0 m and 40.2 m sit inside the 250 m match radius, so neither is a phantom charge and POL-RD-09(4) adds nothing and produces no billing-integrity referral. But because the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) refunds the off-route ERP to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction. The rider did not choose those gantries any more than the driver chose the closure. The correction is $4.00, within the $12.00 cap. POL-RD-09(1) does not bite because no POL-RD-02 refund runs, so nothing is double-counted.

POL-RD-04 (rider-requested detour) does not apply. The only chat messages on EV-CHAT-00103 are the driver's 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' and the rider's 'ok' — an acknowledgment of the driver's choice, not a rider instruction, and the rider's message carries no waypoint_hint, so the corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable. The chat is consistent context and does not move the ERP to the rider.

BURDEN (POL-RD-08). The rider carried the initial burden: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00103, and the unimpaired trace shows an excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold. The driver discharged the shifted burden for the distance and time lines by pointing to a specific advisory ID and clause (EV-ADVIS-00103-01, POL-RD-03); that advisory does not, however, reach the pass-through ERP, which is settled under POL-RD-09(2) as above.

NO ESCALATION. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 175 fixes at a 10.0 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so POL-RD-10(3) is closed. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers match, no timestamp conflict, no missing or mis-scoped exculpatory artifact, the refund is far below $150.00, the evidence is not contradictory, and every charge line matches the trace. No POL-RD-06 pattern is established (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 553 completed trips), so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The ruling is therefore PARTIAL_REFUND of the $4.00 of off-route ERP; the balance of the fare stands.

ruling.explanation: The route deviation is established but fully excused, and the only money that moves is the ERP. For the driver: the trace ran 11.18 km against the 8.2 km booked optimal — an excess of 2.98 km (36.3%) — so both POL-RD-01 tests pass and a deviation is established. It is nonetheless fully exonerated under POL-RD-03: LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00103-01 closes Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd from 05:30 to 12:00 on 14 July 2026 — the same road the booked optimal uses ('Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry') — its window overlaps the trip, and the driven line leaves and rejoins the optimal corridor. The exoneration cap is min(2.98 km, 1.30 × (10.6 − 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km) = 2.98 km, so the whole excess is justified. Because an exculpatory clause fully excuses the deviation, POL-RD-02 does not run and the distance and time charges stand. For the rider: the ERP does not stand. The booked route carries no ERP (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00); both charged gantries — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) $1.00 — are itemised on_optimal_route false, and the trace crosses both (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 40.25 m, inside the 250 m match radius). Under POL-RD-09(2) an exonerated deviation still returns off-route ERP as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00. That is $4.00, and it is refunded. On the driver's notice point: the 08:12 chat (driver 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah'; rider 'ok') shows the rider did not object, but an acknowledgment is not a rider instruction and the rider's message carries no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable on this record, and the chat does not move the ERP onto the rider — the closure, not the chat, is what excuses the distance and time. On the driver's alternative figure of $4.15: running POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal (11.18 km) gives charged 25.12 less recomputed 20.993 = 4.127, rounded to $4.15; that computation applies only where part of the excess is left unexonerated, and none is, so POL-RD-02 does not run and the $4.00 pass-through is not added to any POL-RD-02 figure (POL-RD-09(1)). The gap between the two routes is the 0.4 minutes of trip beyond the adjusted optimal. No repeat-deviation pattern is established (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 553) and the deviation is not material (36.3% and 2.98 km, both under the 50% and 8.0 km thresholds), so no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral follows. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (175 fixes at 10 s, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s), so no POL-RD-07 or POL-RD-10 issue arises, and both ERP lines are matched to the trace, so POL-RD-09(4) adds nothing. Profile fields outside the citable counters are context only under POL-GEN-01. Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of $4.00 against the $9.00 contested.

To the rider: you are right about the ERP, and $4.00 of the $9.00 you contested is returned to you. Braddell Road really was closed that morning — LTA advisory ADV-20260714-031 shut 'Braddell Road (towards Serangoon), between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd' from 05:30 to 12:00, and your 08:07–08:36 trip sits inside that window, with the driven line leaving the closed corridor and rejoining it. The driver's diversion is therefore excused in full under POL-RD-03: measured excess was 2.98 km (trace 11.18 km vs booked optimal 8.2 km — POL-RD-01's trace figure, not the rounded 11.2 copy) and the POL-RD-03 cap is min(2.98, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km, so nothing is left unexonerated. Because the excess is fully excused, POL-RD-02 does not run and the distance and time lines stand — you did travel the extra distance. What you should not pay is the expressway ERP: your booked route carries no gantry at all (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00), and both charges are itemised off-route — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) $1.00, on_optimal_route false, off-optimal total $4.00. POL-RD-09(2) says that where a detour is excused as an external event, off-route ERP is still refunded to you standalone, capped at $12.00. That is $4.00, and it is the whole of this ruling. To the driver: your route is accepted and no distance or time refund is owed. Both gantries were genuinely crossed (nearest trace fixes 0.0 m and 40.2 m, inside the 250 m match radius), so POL-RD-09(4) finds no phantom line and no billing-integrity referral arises. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 553 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral follows, and the deviation was not even MATERIAL (36.3% and 2.98 km are both under the 50% / 8.0 km thresholds). The only money that moves is the government ERP pass-through, which the policy requires be returned to the rider. On the two alternative figures argued: the $8.50 is a POL-RD-02 recomputation against the booked 8.2 km optimal and does not apply because the closure fully exonerates; the $4.15 is a POL-RD-02 recomputation against the closure-adjusted 11.18 km optimal and likewise does not apply, because POL-RD-02 runs only on excess beyond the POL-RD-03 cap and there is none. For transparency the underlying lines are: charged_total 25.12, distance-and-time recomputation not engaged, off-route ERP pass-through correction 4.00 (cap 12.00), refund to rider 4.00. Both parties' submissions on the trace being clean are accepted: 175 fixes at a 10.0 s interval, 100% coverage, max gap 0.0 s, so POL-RD-07 is not engaged and there is no escalation under POL-RD-10. Confidence rests wholly on weight-1.0 artifacts (trip record, GPS trace, fare breakdown, LTA advisory).

ledger.claim: This trip deviates from the route the rider booked. The GPS trace runs 11.18 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 8.2 km — an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.34% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute), so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED, and POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure — 11.18 km, not the rounded 11.2 km convenience copy — the governing measurement.

The rider's complaint is not that a detour happened — the closure explains that — but that the detour cost them ERP they never agreed to. The route they booked carries no ERP at all: trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00, and the routing engine records the optimal route as 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry'. Every cent of the $4.00 of ERP on this fare was created by leaving that no-gantry corridor; none of it belongs to the trip the rider booked.

Both charged gantries are itemised in the fare breakdown as lying off the optimal route: CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at $1.00, each carrying on_optimal_route false, with the breakdown's own on-optimal-route ERP total at $0.00 and its off-optimal-route total at $4.00. The trace confirms the vehicle actually passed both points (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 40.2 m). These are genuine off-route pass-through charges for gantries that form no part of the booked route, and they are precisely what the rider contests.

The LTA DataMall closure EV-ADVIS-00103-01 exonerates the distance and time charges under POL-RD-03: it names Braddell Road between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd, its 05:30–12:00 window overlaps the trip, and its geometry intersects the booked optimal route. But exoneration of the driver's conduct does not shift the government-set pass-through onto the rider. Under POL-RD-09(2), where a deviation is exonerated as an external event, off-route ERP is still refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at SGD 12.00 per trip. The rider did not cause the closure any more than the driver did, and the $4.00 of gantry charges they never chose must come back.

The $4.00 is refundable whichever way the closure is treated, so no reading of the record leaves it with the rider. If POL-RD-03 exoneration applies, POL-RD-09(2) returns it as a pass-through correction. If the judge declines to exonerate, POL-RD-09(1) and POL-RD-02 still return it, because a recomputed fare built on the optimal route (16.63) contains ERP for on-optimal-route gantries only — here 0.00 — so the $4.00 is comprehended inside the refund and is never added on top. Either route to the ruling ends with the rider whole on the ERP.

The driver cannot move this ERP to the rider under POL-RD-04, because the chat runs the other way. At 08:12:30 the driver announced 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah'; the rider's only message is 'ok' at 08:12:58 — an acknowledgment of the driver's choice, not a rider instruction. POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider and to identify a place or road specifically enough to act on, corroborated through chat_message.waypoint_hint; the rider's message carries no waypoint_hint, so the corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable on this record, and POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP refund.

The rider has carried the initial POL-RD-08 burden and it has shifted. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-00103, and the unimpaired trace shows an excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold. To resist, the driver must point to a specific artifact and clause; the only exculpatory artifact on file — the closure advisory — is directed at the distance and time lines, not at the $4.00 of ERP the rider is disputing, and it discharges nothing on those pass-through lines.

The road closure fully exonerates this route under POL-RD-03. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00103-01 (ADV-20260714-031, severity HIGH) closes 'Braddell Road (towards Serangoon), between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd' from 05:30 to 12:00 on 2026-07-14, and the trace window (first fix 08:07:20, last fix 08:36:20) sits squarely inside that window. The POL-RD-03 cap is min(measured excess 2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km) = 2.98 km. The whole of the measured excess is therefore justified, nothing is left unexonerated, and the driver keeps the fare computed on the closure-adjusted optimal.

All three POL-RD-03 conditions are met on this record: (a) the advisory names a road the optimal route traverses - the trip_record's own optimal_route_source is 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry', the same Braddell Road the advisory closes; (b) its validity window overlaps the time the trace shows the vehicle on that segment (intersects_route true, overlaps_trip_window true, overlap_minutes 35.2); and (c) the driven line leaves the optimal corridor and rejoins it, running 11.18 km against an 8.2 km optimal, crossing two CTE gantries each flagged on_optimal_route false, exactly the 'Diversion via Lorong 1 Toa Payoh or CTE' the advisory describes. The driven 11.18 km is within 0.58 km of the 10.6 km shortest lawful alternative, inside the 1.0 km tolerance built into the POL-RD-03 cap.

Because POL-RD-03 fully excuses the excess, POL-RD-02 does not run against the rider's benefit. POL-RD-02 is engaged only where a deviation is established AND 'no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'; here the exculpatory clause excuses 100% of the excess. POL-RD-03 directs POL-RD-02 only to the excess BEYOND the cap, and there is none. The driver was not at fault for an emergency water-main closure, so the distance and time charges stand and no distance-based refund is owed to the rider.

The rider's only recovery is the off-route ERP pass-through under POL-RD-09(2): where the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03 the distance and time charges stand, but off-route ERP is refunded standalone, capped at SGD 12.00. The off-route ERP actually charged is SGD 4.00 (CTE Braddell Rd SGD 3.00 plus CTE Moulmein Rd SGD 1.00, both on_optimal_route false; off_optimal_route_total 4.00, on_optimal_route_total 0.00). The correction is therefore SGD 4.00 - not the SGD 9.00 contested, and not the SGD 8.50 that an UNadjusted POL-RD-02 recomputation against the booked 8.2 km optimal would yield. The closure is worth roughly SGD 4.35 to the driver and that reduction is exactly what POL-RD-03 exists to deliver.

Neither ERP line is a phantom charge, so POL-RD-09(4) adds nothing to the rider's recovery. Under the POL-RD-09 match rule a gantry is treated as crossed where a trace fix lies within 250 m of it: the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry at (1.3401, 103.8496) has a nearest fix at 0.0 m (fix index 33, 08:12:50) and the CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) gantry at (1.324, 103.854) has a nearest fix at 40.25 m (fix index 74, 08:19:40), both well inside the radius, and both charge times (08:14:06 and 08:19:41) fall inside the trace window. There is no unmatched line, no billing-integrity failure, and no ground for a full ERP refund on top of the capped pass-through.

The rider had contemporaneous notice of the diversion and did not object. At 08:12:30 the driver messaged 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' and the rider replied 'ok' at 08:12:58, both read within about 30 seconds; that exchange predates the second gantry charge at 08:19:41. It corroborates that the diversion was the driver's response to the closure, not a route taken against the rider's wishes, and it is consistent with the advisory the platform elsewhere holds.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern and no POL-RD-06 uplift. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 553 - below the 3-flag test and below the 0.05 ratio test - so no pattern is established and neither the FULL_REFUND uplift nor the driver-conduct referral of POL-RD-06 follows. The deviation is in any event not MATERIAL on this trip (36.3% and 2.98 km, both under the 50% and 8.0 km thresholds), so the POL-RD-06 check was not even required. POL-GEN-01 confines any profile use to these named counters; the driver's record is not a ground for an adverse finding.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07, so there is no route to ESCALATE. It carries 175 fixes at a 10.0 s sampling interval with 100% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0; limbs (a) to (c) are not engaged and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation ground is closed. The excess rests on a clean, unbroken trace and the case can and should be decided on this trip's own evidence rather than held for a human reviewer.

Even on the tribunal's alternative reading the rider's recovery is bounded at SGD 4.15. The driver has discharged the POL-RD-08 shifted burden by pointing to a specific advisory ID (EV-ADVIS-00103-01) and a specific clause (POL-RD-03), so the excess is excused rather than refunded. If the tribunal prefers to run POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal of 11.18 km instead, the refund is charged_total 25.12 less recomputed_fare 20.993 = 4.127, rounded up to SGD 4.15 - and that figure already excludes the off-route gantries, so the ERP cannot be counted a second time (POL-RD-09(1)). Either way the rider is far short of the SGD 9.00 contested.
